pageCache.pageTitle: St Martin's CE Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Community, Courage, Aspiration
​​​​​​​St. Martin's
St Martin’s CE Primary Academy is a thriving primary school in the heart of Salisbury city centre and a member of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust. We are one of the most diverse schools in the county and proudly celebrate the many nationalities, religions and cultures that pass through our doors everyday.
Useful Links
Latest News
Follow Us
Our Nursery children had a wonderful adventure in Forest School. The children had so much fun creating their own slides and swings, exploring, taking safe risks and working together. Outdoor play like this builds confidence, creativity and important physical skills all while connecting with nature.
Practicing name writing! So proud of our little learners and their growing confidence.
Sand, water and bubbles fun! Lots of smiles, splashes and sensory play as our children explored, poured and popped!
Our Reception children had a wonderful trip to Salisbury Market today! They explored the stalls, chatted with local traders and carefully chose fresh ingredients for their DT project. It was fantastic to see their confidence growing as they made decisions and handled money. We can't wait to see what delicious creations they make next!
A lovely day out at Riverbourne Community Farm. Our nursery children had such a wonderful visit today, meeting lots of friendly animals and even getting to feed them! It was a truly memorable experience. A hands-on experience full of learning, laughter and fresh air. Days like these are what childhood memories are made of.
Our school-based nursery provides a warm, safe, and stimulating environment where young children learn through play, curiosity, and care. With experienced staff, purpose-built facilities, and a smooth transition into school life, we help every child grow in confidence, independence, and joy. Start your child's next big adventure by calling the school office on 01722 554300 and booking a tour. See our nursery in the Salisbury Journal! https://www.salisburyjournal.co.uk/news/25591499.new-nursery-st-martins-school-salisbury-opened/
We explored writing letters in the sand! Sensory, fun and full of learning. Perfect for building fine motor skills while enjoying a bit of creativity.
Our little learners went on a nature walk to explore and discover all kinds of natural treasures. 🪹🌳 Back in class they used their treasures to create fantastic, nature-inspired artwork. 🍂🌿 Such a fun way to combine exploration and creativity!
We've been celebrating Bonfire Night with some bright and creative artwork! The children loved exploring colours and different materials to capture the magic of fireworks. 🎆🎇🌠
We have been getting creative in the kitchen this week and learning how to use cutlery safely while making some tasty treats!
Our children have been learning all about colours in lots of fun and creative ways! It's amazing to see their curiosity and imagination shine. 🌈🎨
Our builders loved exploring the Three Little Pigs this week. They told stories together, learnt some new special vocabulary and built some houses that were so strong even the Big Bad Wolf couldn't knock them down!
Our school nursery is officially open! Academy CEO, Mark Lacey came to open our nursery and shared a message that all are welcome at St Martin's. The children also planted a special tree as a permanent reminder of our very special first group of nursery students. 🌳💚
Enjoying the Spring sunshine 🌈
​​​​​​​What’s up next?​​​​​​​

pageCache.pageTitle: St Martin's CE Primary School - Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Wherever you go - be strong and courageous
Joshua is a special figure at our school. His long journey and search for a home resonates throughout our community, no matter which religion they follow. Joshua's strength, bravery and unwavering faith in the promises he had been given inspire us to show the same, no matter where we go in life. The courage he showed, the aspirations he had for his life and faith community he built make him a perfect figure for our Biblical Underpinning.
We asked some members of our school community what this verse means to them:
"It felt very different and I felt pretty shy when I came to a new school. I have different classmates and friends now. I feel brave and strong at my new school. Delisha
"Being strong and courageous means never giving up. When I walked in I didn't know half of the class but I had to be brave." Sianna
"This means being brave in ourselves. Doing something kind and helping others is a way we can build our community." Ashwayne
"Wherever you go, be strong, never give up and be kind!" Hareem
Our vision vessel is a map, which reflects the wonderfully diverse journeys that our school community travel on.
Each child has found a place to belong at St Martin's school where they will be welcomed, supported, challenged and celebrated.
Whether they are here for a short stop on their journey or for seven full years, each child who comes through our door will leave our school with truly wonderful experiences to add to their own personal life map.
Our school values, which underpin everything we do at St Martin's Primary:
Listen to St Martin's Worship Council talk about our school values:
Courage
Community
Aspiration
Aspiration
I can do everything through Him who strengthens me
No matter what we aspire to achieve, we know that God is on our team. He gives us strength to aim high, achieve our goals and live out our dreams.
At St Martin’s, we nurture high aspirations uniquely to each child and equip them with the knowledge, resilience and confidence to meet their full potential. We nurture not only to each individual’s highest academic attainment, but also support them to aspire more widely. Children at St Martin’s aspire to help others, to make their mark on the world and to achieve their goals.
Community
Above all, keep loving one another earnestly
Through our value of community, we encourage our children to care for one another as God cares for us. The children of St Martin’s Primary School are from a widely diverse set of individual communities and, by valuing each child for their unique perspective, we build a strong collective, rooted in tolerance, respect and empathy. By prioritising this sense of togetherness, we enable all to flourish together.
Courage
I will show you my faith by my deeds
We are courageous advocates at St Martin’s Primary School – the children speak out for the things that are meaningful to them and use their bravery to teach others from their unique perspective. By instilling courage in the children we teach, we are enabling them to be resilient, capable learners who are ready to take risks and challenge themselves. We teach our children that courage also means being brave enough to be uniquely ourselves and to have the confidence to reach out to others when we need to.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Martin's CE Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
St. Martin's CE Primary Academy is a member of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and a thriving one-form entry primary in the heart of Salisbury city centre. We are one of the most diverse schools in the county and proudly celebrate the many nationalities, religions and cultures that pass through our doors everyday.
My name is Ollie Martindale and I have worked in education for 18 years. I have been Executive Headteacher here at St. Martin's since September 2024 and played a significant role at the school during the previous summer term. I feel privileged to be working alongside such ambitious, creative and caring children, as well as the many dedicated professionals working in and out of classrooms here at St. Martin's.
For the previous six years, I led - and continue to lead in my role as Executive Headteacher - at St. Peter's CE Primary Academy. We achieved a very positive OFSTED in November 2022 and the school continues to grow both in size and reputation. My ambition for St. Martin's is the same and the drive to achieve such positive outcomes resonated with several other colleagues who moved from St. Peter's to St. Martin's. One such person is our Head of School here, Mrs Miller-Goddard. You'd be hard pushed to find a more passionate and inclusive educator, and she is someone that prospective and existing parents will always find at the gates in the morning welcoming our children in. Mrs M-G has taught in schools for over 10 years and has an outstanding track record of school improvement in the many roles she has assumed (including SENDCo and Assistant Headteacher).
In addition to myself and Mrs. M-G, St. Martin's has recruited a new Deputy Headteacher, SENDCo and several teachers in the past six months. We are an ambitious and effective team supported by an equally accomplished Trust, and I would encourage any potential parents to visit us to see our amazing children in situ, to see the reality of life at St. Martin's. Most importantly, you'd see children that are happy, safe and enjoying the challenge of their learning.
Mr Ollie Martindale NPQEL
Executive Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: St Martin's CE Primary School - Wraparound Care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Breakfast Club
8am - 8.40am - £2 per child
Two of our wonderful support assistants run our fun and friendly breakfast club, which offers children a healthy breakfast, including toast, crumpets, fruit and a drink. Pupils can then enjoy a calm activity, such as lego or arts/crafts, before they are taken down to class.
Breakfast club is run in the school hall. Parents/pupils can access the club via the playground gates near reception.
To book for your child to attend, please do this via your Arbor app, if you require any support with this, please do get in touch with the office.
After School Club
3.20pm - 4.00pm - £3.00 per child
Our highly trained staff provide after school care to all families who need a later collection time. Children will have a range of activities to choose from, including arts/crafts, sport or technology. All children are given a drink and snack during the session.
To book for your child to attend, please do this via your Arbor app, if you require any support with this, please do get in touch with the office.
Wider Club Offer
Every term, we offer a variety of clubs, including sports, arts and crafts, cookery and chess. These are advertised to parents and pupils in a letter and booked in advance via Arbor. Some of these clubs are funded by the school and offered free of charge to parents. We ask for a small charge for some clubs to cover the cost of resources.

Personal Development
Personal Development at St Martin’s
At St Martin’s CE Primary School, personal development is woven through every aspect of school life. Our carefully planned and sequenced Personal Development Curriculum brings together the opportunities pupils receive within and beyond the academic curriculum throughout their time with us.
We want every child to develop the knowledge, character and confidence they need to flourish. Through a wide range of purposeful experiences, pupils learn how to build positive relationships, care for their physical and emotional wellbeing, understand and respect different people and cultures, and contribute positively to their community and the wider world.
Our provision reflects the needs of our pupils and our diverse school community. We actively remove barriers so that all children, including pupils with SEND, those learning English as an additional language and those who may have fewer opportunities beyond school, can participate fully. Pupils are encouraged to discover their interests and talents while developing resilience, independence, aspiration and the courage to try new things.
The Intent of our Personal Development Curriculum
Every person, every opportunity, every day

These five areas provide a coherent structure through which pupils develop personally, socially, morally, spiritually and culturally. pageCache.pageTitle: St Martin's CE Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Information About Our Curriculum
for 2-3 Year Olds
for 3-4 Year Olds
At St. Martin’s Nursery, our carefully designed curriculum is built around the principle that every child deserves a rich and nurturing start to their educational journey. Grounded in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework and enhanced by our own curriculum priorities, we create an environment that balances structured learning with the freedom to explore. Our youngest learners (aged 2–4) are supported to develop prime skills in communication, personal and emotional development, and physical coordination, ensuring a strong foundation for future learning. Through a thoughtful balance of adult-led activities and child-initiated play, we celebrate each child’s individuality, interests, and needs.
Being part of a wider school setting means our nursery children benefit from the expertise of highly experienced teachers who understand the full arc of a child's educational journey. Our team is uniquely placed to ensure that pupils are truly “school ready” by the time they transition to Reception, developing not only strong early literacy and numeracy skills but also essential learning behaviours such as curiosity, resilience, and independence. Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that early concepts are built on year after year, ensuring continuity, progression, and success. Children also enjoy a rich outdoor learning programme, where they explore and develop skills in our nursery garden and wider outdoor spaces, fostering a sense of curiosity, confidence, and connection with the natural world.
At St. Martin’s, we believe education should be holistic, nurturing the whole child. Alongside academic preparation, we prioritise children’s emotional wellbeing, social development, creativity, and love of learning. We offer exciting opportunities for off-site visits, including trips to Riverbourne Farm and the library at Godolphin School, broadening children's experiences and strengthening their understanding of the wider community. Our nursery is a welcoming and vibrant space where strong, trusting relationships are at the heart of everything we do. This close link between nursery and school provides an exceptional start for children and families alike, embedding a sense of belonging and laying the groundwork for a lifelong love of learning.

Curriculum
Curriculum Intent
At St Martin’s CE Primary Academy our curriculum is designed to provide an ambitious, broad and knowledge rich education that prepares pupils for the next stage of their learning and for life beyond school. We know that excellent teaching underpins the successful delivery of our curriculum, which is why we prioritise our Five Pillars of Excellent Teaching in every classroom, every lesson and every day. Excellent teaching is central to our curriculum design.
Our curriculum is ambitious, inclusive and designed to ensure that every pupil develops the knowledge and skills needed to succeed. Learning is carefully sequenced from pupils’ starting points so that essential knowledge builds securely and pupils are well prepared for each stage of their education.
We place a strong emphasis on English, mathematics, religious education and science. These subjects are taught discretely through clearly structured and progressive programmes of study. Across the wider curriculum, pupils develop secure subject knowledge alongside the communication, reasoning and enquiry skills that enable them to think and work within each discipline.
Teachers have high expectations for all pupils and make purposeful adaptations so that pupils with SEND, those learning English as an additional language and pupils who may face other barriers can access the same ambitious curriculum and achieve well. Regular assessment helps teachers identify gaps, check that important knowledge has been remembered and provide timely support.
Our curriculum reflects the needs, experiences and diversity of our pupils while broadening their understanding of the wider world. It promotes curiosity, confidence and independence and prepares children to flourish in the next stage of their education and beyond.
We work closely with families to support pupils’ learning. Parents and carers are invited to regular curriculum workshops that explain how learning is structured and provide practical ways to support children at home.

pageCache.text:
SEND
St. Martin’s CE Primary School is committed to providing a high-quality education for all the children in our school. We believe that all children have a common entitlement to a broad and balanced academic and social curriculum which is accessible to them, and to be fully included in all aspects of school life. All children can make outstanding progress, and we move each child from their individual starting points. We have high expectations of all children. Regardless of ability, every child’s progress is regularly checked and any child who appears to be stuck is acknowledged and enabled to move forward again.
The Local Authority's Local Offer
For any queries about Wiltshire’s SEND Service or information about supporting children and young people with SEND, please call the Single Point of Access (SPA) on 0300 247 0090.
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCo) is Mrs Sally Abbott, who co-ordinates and supports staff to deliver high quality SEN provision within the school. For more information regarding SEND, please read our information report below, which details our approach within school and who to contact if you have any concerns.
